title: Konbaung Dynasty
capsule: The Konbaung dynasty was founded in 1752 by Alaungpaya, a Shwebo headman who rallied resistance to the Mon-led Restored Hanthawaddy Kingdom and had reunified Burma by 1759. The dynasty built the largest empire in Burmese history: Alaungpaya's son Hsinbyushin definitively sacked Ayutthaya in 1767 while repelling four Qing invasions (1765-69), and Bodawpaya later turned westward, annexing Arakan (1784), Manipur (1814), and Assam (1817). By around 1820 Konbaung Burma had reached its greatest territorial extent, its expansion now pressing directly against British India along an ill-defined frontier that would soon ignite the first of the Anglo-Burmese Wars. The court also sponsored major literary, legal, and Buddhist codifications.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Burmese territories are well documented; frontier zones with China, Siam, and Manipur fluctuated considerably across the dynasty's history, and the attestation window here (1741–1820) predates the major British annexations, requiring period-specific boundary reconstruction.
